# Guard the Flock

> An independent educational and support resource for the Christian Church and faith communities to recognise, understand, and recover from spiritual abuse, discern healthy biblical leadership, and find trusted help.

## About Guard the Flock

Guard the Flock helps individuals, church members, and pastoral leaders understand spiritual abuse and religious coercive control. It provides definitions, behavioural red flags, biblical discernment frameworks, practical safety and recovery guidance, and documented public case studies.

## Key Sections

The website is a single-page resource with tab-based navigation. These links use section anchors that open the relevant tab:

- [Understand Spiritual Abuse](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#understand-what): Definitions, forms of spiritual abuse, theological manipulation, coercive control, and why people may remain silent.
- [Warning Signs & Discernment](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#discern-signs): Common warning signs, patterns of control, and tests for discerning healthy from harmful leadership.
- [Get Help / Respond](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#respond-intro): Practical steps, support options, documentation, and guidance for responding to concerns.
- [For Church Leaders](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#leaders-top): Healthy pastoral care, disclosure response, governance safeguards, and leadership self-audit.
- [Documented Cases](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#cases-top): Publicly documented cases, source material, and lessons about institutional accountability.
- [Study & Resources](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#study-top): Bible study material, recommended resources, and further reading.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://guardtheflock.pages.dev/#faq-anchor): Answers to common questions about spiritual abuse, biblical discernment, and responding to concerns.

## Biblical Foundations

- **1 Peter 5:2–3**: Shepherd God's flock willingly and eagerly, not for dishonest gain, and do not lord authority over those entrusted to you; be examples to the flock.
- **Ezekiel 34**: A prophetic warning against self-serving shepherds who exploit the vulnerable instead of strengthening the weak and caring for the wounded.
- **Matthew 20:25–28**: Jesus contrasts servant leadership with leaders who lord authority over others.

## Helplines & Support Directory

The website's Get Help / Respond section lists support resources and practical guidance. Availability and suitability vary by location; readers should check the relevant provider's current information. The site is an educational resource, not an emergency service, counselling provider, or independent investigative body.
